title: What If a Carrington Solar Storm Hit Us Today?

scenes.text: What if the 1859 solar storm hit tonight? Last time, telegraph wires caught fire.
A cloud of solar plasma crosses 150 million kilometers to Earth in about eighteen hours. In 1859 it took 17.6.
The sky would blaze. In 1859 auroras reached Cuba, and people read newspapers by their light.
Wires sparked and operators were shocked. Some telegraphs even sent messages with their batteries unplugged.
Today, Lloyd's of London has estimated losses of up to 2.6 trillion dollars in North America, with blackouts possibly lasting years.
In 2012 a storm just as strong missed Earth by about nine days. Back in 1859, it only had telegraphs to break.

description:
What if a Carrington-class solar storm hit us today?
Auroras in the tropics, and a grid that may not survive it.
